title: A Fishing Trawler at the Pier
description: Explore the equipment and spaces of a working fishing boat beside its landing place.
cardDescription: Explore the equipment and spaces of a working fishing boat beside its landing place.
subtheme: A Fishing Trawler at the Pier
focus: A trawler tows a net, while other fishing vessels use different methods. The clues separate the catch-handling equipment, storage area, and upper working surfaces.
solvingTip: Use the equipment’s task: towing, lifting, holding a catch, or securing the vessel.
words: Fishing vessel equipped to tow a large collecting net
Powered drum mechanism used to haul a cable aboard a boat
Large net towed through water or near the seabed
Storage space below a fishing vessel's deck
Floating marker attached to fishing gear or marking a location
Mesh equipment used to collect fish
Strong line used for hauling a heavy fishing net
Open working floor on a fishing vessel
Upright support rising above a fishing boat
Rigid container used for handling a landed catch
Frozen water used to keep a catch cool
Flexible line used to secure the boat at a pier
People operating the fishing vessel together
Waterfront structure beside which the boat lands

answerNotes.TRAWLER: Trawling uses a towed net; it differs from fishing with a hook and line or setting pots.
answerNotes.WINCH: A winch winds or releases line under control; it differs from the cable itself.
answerNotes.TRAWL: Trawl names the net or method; the vessel equipped for the work is a trawler.
answerNotes.HOLD: A hold is a compartment for cargo or catch, not the open working surface above it.
answerNotes.BUOY: A buoy floats at the surface; it can mark equipment or serve other navigational purposes.

title: Where the River Meets the Sea
description: Explore an estuary through its mixture of waters, sheltered shores, and changing tidal surfaces.
cardDescription: Explore an estuary through its mixture of waters, sheltered shores, and changing tidal surfaces.
subtheme: Where the River Meets the Sea
focus: An estuary receives both river water and marine influence. Salinity and water levels can vary across it, so the clues describe its processes and landforms rather than one fixed condition.
solvingTip: Distinguish a water property from a landform or a moving process.
words: Coastal area where fresh river water mixes with seawater
Describing water saltier than fresh water but less salty than seawater
Broad muddy surface exposed when tidal water recedes
Fine sediment that may settle where flowing water slows
Dissolved substance contributing to seawater's salinity
Periodic change in coastal water level
Narrow opening allowing water into a coastal area
Wetland with soft-stemmed vegetation near shallow water
Deeper passage through an estuary used by flowing water or boats
Land along the edge of the estuary
Tall waterside plant growing in some wetland margins
Movement of river water toward the coast
Place where a river opens into a larger body of water
Land bordering a river near its lower reaches

answerNotes.ESTUARY: An estuary combines river and marine influences; its salt content can vary with location, tide, and river flow.
answerNotes.BRACKISH: Brackish describes intermediate salinity, not one exact salt concentration everywhere.
answerNotes.MUDFLAT: A mudflat is periodically covered and uncovered; it is not necessarily permanently dry ground.
answerNotes.SILT: Silt describes a particle-size category between sand and clay rather than all mud in general.
answerNotes.SALT: Salt content helps distinguish freshwater and marine influence within an estuary.

title: A Wooden Rowboat by the Dock
description: Find the familiar parts and supplies around a small wooden rowboat at the dock.
cardDescription: Find the familiar parts and supplies around a small wooden rowboat at the dock.
subtheme: A Wooden Rowboat by the Dock
focus: An oar moves the boat through the water. Seats, ropes, and a bucket belong to the ordinary dockside scene.
solvingTip: The short tool and container clues can help with boat-part words.
words: Small boat moved through the water with oars
Long-handled tool pulled through water to move this boat
Front end of the wooden boat
Boat's main body, including its bottom and sides
Place where a person sits while rowing
Thick line used to tie the boat to the dock
Colored coating brushed onto the boat's surface
Opening that lets unwanted water into the boat
Long flat piece of wood used in the boat's body
Platform beside which the rowboat is tied
Large inland body of water where a rowboat may travel
Handled container used to carry or scoop water

answerNotes.ROWBOAT: A rowboat gets its name from how it is propelled.
answerNotes.OAR: An oar works as a lever against the water.
answerNotes.BOW: Bow identifies the forward end, opposite the stern.
answerNotes.STERN: The stern is the rear end rather than either side.
answerNotes.HULL: The hull is the boat's body, not its loose equipment.

title: Buoys Beyond the Harbor
description: Recognize floating navigation aids through their lights, sounds, and mooring equipment.
cardDescription: Recognize floating navigation aids through their lights, sounds, and mooring equipment.
focus: A buoy can carry a light, a sound device, or scientific instruments. The clues name its parts and signals without turning the puzzle into route-planning instructions.
solvingTip: Identify whether the clue asks for the whole floating object, a signal, or a connection below the water.
words: Anchored floating object used as a marker or instrument platform
Visible guiding signal or navigational marker
Anchoring arrangement keeping a buoy in position
Moving piece that strikes the inside of a buoy's bell
Surface that sends incoming light or radar energy back
Metal sounding device carried by some navigation buoys
Visible night signal on an illuminated buoy
Linked metal line connecting buoy and mooring equipment
Heavy or gripping device holding a buoy's mooring
To remain supported at the surface of water
Brief light burst in a repeated signal sequence
Watertight main body of a floating navigation aid
Optical part shaping a buoy lamp's outgoing light
To identify a location using a visible navigation aid

answerNotes.BUOY: A buoy floats while held in position or deployed for a task; its purpose can be navigation or measurement.
answerNotes.BEACON: Beacon is broader than buoy: a beacon may be fixed on land or on a structure rather than floating.
answerNotes.MOORING: A mooring joins the floating object to its holding arrangement below; it is separate from the light above.
answerNotes.CLAPPER: A bell makes its sound when struck; a clapper is the striking component rather than the entire bell.
answerNotes.REFLECTOR: A reflector returns an incoming signal; it differs from a lamp that emits its own visible light.

title: Reading a Harbor Chart
description: Examine a nautical chart through its depth marks, symbols, and the words for places beside the water.
cardDescription: Examine a nautical chart through its depth marks, symbols, and the words for places beside the water.
focus: A nautical chart represents navigation-related features and measured water depths. It differs in purpose from a general road map, and its reference information matters when interpreting a measurement.
solvingTip: Use the clue’s category: a number, a reference, a land feature, or a water passage.
words: Navigation drawing showing water depths and coastal features
Measured water depth marked on a nautical chart
Reference level or surface used for chart measurements
Key explaining symbols used on a nautical chart
Direction to a point expressed relative to a reference
Vertical distance from the water surface to the bottom
Rock or coral feature lying at or near the sea surface
Shallow underwater area represented on a chart
Narrow water opening leading inland from the coast
Land surrounded by water on a chart
Relationship between chart distance and actual distance
Land bordering the sea along the chart's edge
Harbor town or place where vessels load and unload
Compass ___, directional diagram printed on many charts

answerNotes.CHART: A nautical chart includes information useful on the water; it serves a different purpose from an ordinary road map.
answerNotes.SOUNDING: A sounding is a depth measurement; the chart's stated units and reference level determine how to interpret its number.
answerNotes.DATUM: A datum supplies a reference, not a depth reading by itself.
answerNotes.LEGEND: A legend explains the marks; it is different from the chart's geographical scale.
answerNotes.BEARING: A bearing describes direction, while range describes distance in many navigation contexts.
